title: Singustars: Between Black Holes and Compact Stars
summary: The Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff equations admit singular solutions in which a negative point mass is surrounded by a self-gravitating fluid. For a $Γ$-law polytropic equation of state, these solutions, which we call singustars, are thick shells bounded by two zero-pressure surfaces around a naked, repulsive, negative-mass singularity, with a Schwarzschild exterior. They form a two-parameter family, labeled by the mass $M$ and the compactness $C\equiv M/R$. Singustars join regular polytropes as the central negative mass vanishes and reach compactness beyond the Buchdahl bound. From exact equilibria and their radial modes, we find that singustars with $Γ= 2$ are stable only for $M\lesssim0.63$ and $C\lesssim0.25$, a region that nonetheless contains configurations more compact than any stable regular polytrope, although none with a light ring. In the numerically resolved parameter space, unstable singustars have a single unstable radial mode; many are energetically unbound. Nonlinear evolutions in ingoing null coordinates show that the end state depends on the perturbation. For the collapsing models studied, backward tracing of outgoing null rays identifies an event-horizon generator with a past endpoint on the singularity, before the first trapped surface appears. Outward perturbations disperse unbound shells and leave the singularity naked, while a bound shell migrates toward, and oscillates about, a stable configuration with the same conserved masses.

title: Gravitational radiation from a particle in circular orbit around a wormhole: the nonrotating case
summary: In this paper, we have generalized Poisson's(1993) calculation for the case of gravitational radiation from a particle in a circular orbit around a black hole to the case of the wormhole. Considering the motion of a test particle around a Schwarzschild like wormhole and using Teukolsky formalism, we have obtained an analytical result of flux at infinity under the assumption of small velocities. Focusing on the 22-mode, we have found a novel 0.5PN order term beyond the quadrupole order, which vanishes in the black hole limit. On the other hand, all higher order terms are getting modified in such a way that they give correct correspondence in the black hole limit. We have further corroborated our results with the numerical investigations, which show that the two waveforms match well when the particle lies far from ISCO. Thus, our work provides one of the first attempts toward the study of the post-Newtonian waveforms involving wormholes (ECOs).

title: Spectral Constraints on Line-Seed Inverse-Compton Models for the MeV Feature in GRB 221009A
summary: We investigate inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of atomic and molecular line photons as an explanation of the evolving MeV spectral feature observed by Fermi-GBM in GRB 221009A. Detections of H$α$ and Pa$α$ emission from the host galaxy motivate hydrogen recombination seeds, with only indirect support for Ly$α$. A marginal Mg XII feature in the late-time X-ray afterglow provides an event-specific motivation for metal-line seeds, whereas Si XIV, S XVI and iron K-shell transitions are motivated by historical reports of X-ray line features in other gamma-ray bursts. Strong late-time H$_2$ emission detected by the James Webb Space Telescope at the projected burst position motivates our most detailed spectral test. Assuming lateral illumination by the H$_2$ $1-0\,S(1)$ transition at $2.122\,μ{\rm m}$, we calibrate lognormal electron distributions to reproduce the observed MeV photon centroids and widths. We also require IC emission from the ultraviolet (UV) photons driving molecular fluorescence to remain compatible with contemporaneous LAT observations. In a separate test including accompanying molecular transitions, the most favourable configuration, based on the Rh3o photodissociation-region model, approximately describes the MeV feature, although all tested configurations exceed the adopted central spectral references at some energies. For an assumed precursor UV budget, favourable interception substantially reduces the seed-photon energy deficit, but even under ideal excitation and internal escape assumptions, the reference-line photon density in the compact examples falls short of the required value by factors of approximately 4-9. Collisional de-excitation, infrared photon escape and electron cooling impose additional constraints on these configurations. Atomic candidates remain kinematically possible, but their local seed-photon supply is also unestablished.

title: Analysis Methodology of the Search for Ultrahigh Energy Neutrinos in 10.6 Years of Askaryan Radio Array Data
summary: The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA) is an in-ice radio observatory at the South Pole designed to detect ultrahigh energy (UHE) neutrinos through Askaryan emission produced by interactions of neutrinos and their secondary particles. In this paper, we present the detailed methodology of the first array-wide search for a diffuse UHE neutrino flux using data from all five ARA stations. The dataset considered represents $10.6$ years of livetime and is three times larger than previous ARA neutrino searches. This search achieves a $28\%$ analysis efficiency for a neutrino flux corresponding to the current experimental upper limits. No neutrino candidates are observed on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. We set a new upper limit on the diffuse UHE neutrino flux, which is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV. We also discuss lessons learned for future searches on large radio arrays.

title: Black Holes beyond General Relativity: The Effective Metric Description
summary: Black holes provide a privileged window on gravity in the strong-field regime, and deviations from the classical solutions of General Relativity (GR) may encode information about quantum gravity and other extensions of the theory. The abundance of proposed deformed black hole geometries, however, makes model-by-model comparison with observations impractical. This review presents a unified account of the Effective Metric Description (EMD), a model-independent framework in which deformations of static, spherically symmetric black hole spacetimes are parametrized by physical, coordinate-invariant quantities, such as the proper radial distance from the event horizon or the proper time of a free-falling observer. After reviewing the classical black hole solutions and the open issues that motivate going beyond GR, we develop the EMD as a series expansion near the horizon for a given physical quantity. We provide the general solution of the resulting self-consistency conditions compatible with the symmetries of the geometry, derive universal regularity conditions ensuring a finite Hawking temperature and curvature invariants, establish the equivalence of descriptions based on different physical quantities, and extend the framework to charged, extremal and lower-dimensional black holes. Padé resummation extends the description away from the horizon, enabling model-independent computations of the black hole shadow and, in the eikonal limit, of quasi-normal mode frequencies in the test-field approximation. The framework is tested on a broad set of geometries used to model physics beyond GR, and compared with other model-independent parametrizations through explicit transformation maps. As an effective description of deformations beyond GR, the EMD provides a coherent bridge between fundamental black hole physics, quantum-gravity-inspired deformations, and astrophysical observables.

title: New Constraints on the Ultrahigh Energy Neutrino Flux from the First Array-Wide Search with the Askaryan Radio Array
summary: Ultrahigh energy neutrinos ($E_ν\gtrsim 100$ PeV) are detectable through Askaryan emission---the nanosecond-scale radio impulse emitted by relativistic particle cascades in a dielectric medium. The Askaryan Radio Array (ARA), an Askaryan detector array located at the South Pole, has been taking data for more than a decade. We present the first array-wide search for diffuse ultrahigh energy neutrinos with ARA. The search found no events on an expected background of $0.13\pm0.01\text{ (stat.)}^{+0.05}_{-0.06}\text{ (syst.)}$ events. The resulting upper limit is the most stringent from $50$ EeV to $1000$ EeV and provides the first constraints on the flux reported by the KM3NeT Collaboration that are complementary to optical Cherenkov and particle detectors. This limit also constrains UHECR source models, and excludes some models with trans-GZK proton populations at the $90\%$ confidence level. This represents the largest Askaryan detector dataset ever analyzed, demonstrating the feasibility and sensitivity of searches with large detector arrays acting as a single observatory. It also underscores the high acceptance and exposure of Askaryan detector arrays to ultrahigh energy neutrinos.

title: Dynamical obstructions to primary Proca hair and its logarithmic Maxwell continuation
summary: We examine the dynamical admissibility of primary black hole hair in a regularized vector theory of Gauss--Bonnet gravity. The original nontrivial constant norm family cannot satisfy both positive dipole kinetic energy and real nondegenerate radial tensor characteristics. A regular Hamiltonian reduction treats the degenerate boundaries. For asymptotically flat exteriors on the nondegenerate radial branch, adding a Maxwell term for the same vector requires a varying norm. Its positive logarithmic continuation has finite mass at spatial infinity and numerically constructed regular future horizons. The constructed backgrounds satisfy the radial tensor and transverse vector conditions at the sampled points. However, the constrained even angular system has a longitudinal mode with negative squared angular speed. We derive its inverse logarithm coefficient, including both the vector constraint and quartic interaction, and verify it using independent gauge reductions and the full backgrounds. This local angular obstruction persists despite the compatible radial conditions.

title: Leveraging Lensing-driven Early Warnings: Joint Detectability of lensed Gravitational Waves and their LSST Optical Counterparts
summary: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) can be leveraged to provide early-warning times of $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{hours})$ to $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{days})$ prior to the mergers of binary neutron stars (BNSs) and neutron star-black holes (NSBHs). This capability could, in turn, enable electromagnetic (EM) observatories to capture transient emissions surrounding the time of the merger. In this work, we demonstrate the viability of jointly detecting gravitationally lensed BNS and NSBH mergers via GWs during the O5 observing run, alongside their associated kilonova counterparts using the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST). We simulate a population of lensed BNS and NSBH mergers detectable during O5 and utilize current benchmark forward models to generate the corresponding lensed kilonova light curves. We then assess the detectability of these light curves across LSST bands under various exposure limits. We find that among the detectable lensed mergers in O5, approximately 60\% of the BNS kilonova and 10\% of the NSBH kilonova will be observable within a single LSST exposure, with mostly quads dominating the detectable population. Furthermore, we define a detectability index ($\rm DI$), which determines the EM-detectability in optical of lensed GW-detectable BNS and NSBH mergers. We demonstrate the robustness and generalizability of the $\rm DI$ on our lensed BNS and NSBH population. Our work demonstrates that lensing-driven early warnings will be highly applicable in the near future, enabling the LSST to effectively follow up on BNS and NSBH triggers within GW localization areas during the O5 observing run.

title: Perturbative QCD Constraints on Hot Neutron-Star Matter
summary: Perturbative QCD, supplemented only by thermodynamic consistency, causality, and mechanical stability, constrains the equation of state of dense matter far below the densities at which the perturbative expansion itself converges. Until now, however, such constraints have been established only for cold, catalyzed matter. We show that this model-independent bound generalizes to finite temperature along adiabats labelled by the entropy per baryon $\hat{s}$, with the specific enthalpy $h=(\varepsilon+p)/n_{\mathrm{B}}$ assuming the role played by the baryon chemical potential at $T=0$. We find that increasing the temperature shrinks the allowed region monotonically in a form that is universal across structurally distinct mean-field families. For DD2, the density at which the equation of state becomes inconsistent with perturbative QCD decreases from $1.0$ to $0.74\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$ as $\hat{s}$ increases from $0$ to $5$, falling below the central density of the heaviest cold star. By $\hat{s}=4$, seven of eleven relativistic mean-field models are excluded at $6\,n_{\mathrm{sat}}$; approximately half of the equations of state drawn from two Bayesian posteriors are excluded by $\hat{s}\simeq3.4$--$4.4$. When mapped onto the QCD phase diagram, the bound becomes active at temperatures of $100$--$150$ MeV, precisely the regime transiently realized in neutron-star mergers and proto-neutron stars.

title: Images of Regular Black Holes with Hedgehog Scalar Hair Embedded in Radiatively Inefficient Accretion Flows
summary: How a black hole's geometric critical scale manifests in an accretion-flow image is governed by photon propagation, plasma radiative processes, and instrumental resolution. In this work, we investigate radiatively inefficient accretion flows (RIAF) surrounding geometrically regular black holes with hedgehog scalar hair. Adopting the mass and distance of $\mathrm{M87}^*$, we generate total-intensity synchrotron images and systematically explore the viewing inclination, disk thickness, and observing frequency. For the fiducial setup at $230\,\mathrm{GHz}$, raising $L/M$ from $0$ to $0.9$ contracts the critical curve diameter by $4.78\%$, shrinks the half-flux radius by $4.07\%$, and lowers the required electron-density scale by $9.15\%$. At $84\,\mathrm{GHz}$, the primary brightness peaks shift farther outside the critical curve due to enhanced synchrotron self-absorption, whereas the sharper emission rings at $230$ and $345\,\mathrm{GHz}$ closely trace the critical curve. Ultimately, we find that although the regular core systematically contracts the emission ring and alters the required plasma density, resolving these deviations from a Schwarzschild black hole demands angular resolution finer than that achievable with current baselines.

title: Can torsion mimic a cosmological constant? A one-parameter logarithmic $f(T)$ extension of $Λ$CDM
summary: We study a modified teleparallel gravity model of the $f(T)$ type. We propose a new functional form for in order to obtain a geometric origin to the $ΛCDM$ behavior in an appropriate limit. A perturbative expansion around the $ΛCDM$ regime is carried out, and the model's cosmic dynamics are calculated inside the flat FLRW background. By employing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using multiple observational datasets, such as Cosmic Chronometers, Type Ia Supernova compilations (DES-SN5YR, Pantheon+SH0ES, and Union 3.0), DESI DR2 BAO measurements, and Planck 2018 CMB distance priors, to constrain the model parameters. The findings show that the suggested $f(T)$ model accurately replicates the observed accelerated expansion and is statistically consistent with current cosmological observations. The model stays close to the $ΛCDM$ scenario while permitting tiny dynamical adjustments, as evidenced by the extra parameter $γ$, which quantifies deviations from the conventional cosmological model, being limited to values near zero.

title: Simulation-Based Inference on EMRI Frequency Tracks: Harmonic Identification and Parameter Constraints from Search Outputs
summary: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRIs) are key targets for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, but their long, multi-harmonic waveforms make search and parameter estimation computationally expensive. A promising alternative is to work directly with frequency tracks recovered by a time-frequency search pipeline. We investigate whether such tracks can be used to (i) identify which harmonic(s) a recovered track corresponds to, and (ii) constrain the intrinsic EMRI parameters, including when tracks are partially masked near plunge. We first train Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) networks on large banks of azimuthal and radial fundamental-frequency tracks. For harmonic identification, we combine pairs of candidate tracks under different harmonic-label assumptions and use the resulting posterior medians and network acceptance rates to classify the correct labelling. For parameter identification, we apply a sequential (truncated-prior) SBI scheme and refine the results by cross-checking posterior samples against a time-frequency detection statistic. The correct harmonic pair is among the top-2 ranked candidates with probability $>0.99$ across masking levels, and is identified outright in 98% of cases when restricted to physically plausible candidates. Sequential SBI shrinks the intrinsic-parameter prior volume by up to $10^{13}$ within a few hours of GPU time, and the detection-statistic refinement reduces it by up to four further orders of magnitude, even for heavily masked tracks. Frequency-track-based SBI thus provides a fast, waveform-free way to identify EMRI harmonics and obtain tight prior volumes for targeted follow-up, substantially reducing the burden on subsequent MCMC-based analyses.

title: Relativistic tidal response and mode excitation in neutron-star binaries
summary: Tidal excitation links gravitational-wave emission to the internal dynamics of neutron stars. We study the dynamical tidal response of nonrotating stars with composition stratification, elastic crusts and possible first-order phase transitions. Using analytical Mano--Suzuki--Takasugi exterior solutions, we match stellar perturbations to an effective field theory and extract the poles and residues of the relativistic tidal response. Over the inspiral band, this response is accurately approximated by a sum of harmonic oscillators, as in Newtonian theory, each specified by a frequency $ω_α$ and a mode-specific tidal deformability $λ_α$, or equivalently a tidal overlap $I_α$. We couple these oscillators to relativistic effective-one-body dynamics, including gravitational redshift and frame dragging, to follow mode excitation and gravitational-wave emission. A decomposition into driven and free oscillations gives analytical mode amplitudes accurate to a few percent during inspiral. We also reconstruct the time-dependent crustal strain. In a representative $1.20+1.50\,M_\odot$ hadronic--hybrid binary, gravity, interface and shear modes produce a gravitational-wave phase shift of $\lesssim10^{-2}\,{\rm rad}$. Despite this small phase shift, gravity-mode excitation can overstrain the crust near its base, while the lowest shear mode produces widespread overstrain.

title: Unveiling the Extreme Universe with Recent IACT Discoveries
summary: Very-high-energy (VHE, $E \gtrsim 50$\,GeV) $γ$-ray astronomy has evolved into an indispensable pillar of modern astroparticle physics, offering a direct view of non-thermal particle acceleration, cosmic-ray origins, and fundamental physics. Ground-based Imaging Atmospheric Cherenkov Telescopes (IACTs) have driven this revolution over the past two decades. In this plenary review, presented at the 9th Heidelberg International Symposium on High-Energy Gamma-Ray Astronomy (Gamma 2026), I provide a synthesis of recent breakthrough physics discoveries achieved by current IACT arrays (H.E.S.S., MAGIC, and VERITAS) alongside early scientific achievements from the Large-Sized Telescope prototype (LST-1) of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO). Key highlights include the definitive establishment of recurrent novae as transient cosmic-ray proton accelerators via RS Ophiuchi; spatially resolved multi-TeV emission from the relativistic jet termination shocks of microquasars; the discovery of a 20 TeV pulsed radiation component from the Vela pulsar, challenging established magnetospheric emission paradigms; precision measurements of the Galactic Center diffuse ridge spectrum favoring a high-energy cutoff; the detection of distant flat-spectrum radio quasars at $z \sim 1$ (OP 313 and PKS 0346-27), providing tight cosmological constraints on the Extragalactic Background Light; multi-wavelength afterglow detections of $γ$-ray bursts including GRB 221009A; and world-leading joint indirect dark matter limits from dwarf spheroidal galaxy and Galactic Center halo analyses. Together with algorithmic advances in deep learning reconstruction and the ongoing construction of CTAO, these milestones demonstrate the enduring vitality and future trajectory of ground-based $γ$-ray astrophysics.

title: Probing for anisotropies at different angular scales in the arrival directions of the cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory
summary: Studies of the arrival-direction distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays are crucial for revealing their origin. In this work, we investigate the distribution of the arrival directions of events detected with the Pierre Auger Observatory over different angular scales. To do this, we adopt a novel method where we use a von Mises--Fisher distribution to model the excesses with respect to isotropic expectations. This method allows us to study the distribution of arrival directions over different angular scales consistently and simultaneously. We consider the events in different energy bins above 4 EeV detected from 1$^\text{st}$ January 2004 to 31$^\text{st}$ December 2022, i.e. during the entire Phase~I of the Pierre Auger Observatory, with a total exposure of $123{,}000$ km$^2$ sr yr. The most significant excess in the bins considered is a dipolar modulation in the energy range (8--16) EeV, which is compatible with previous findings of the Pierre Auger Collaboration. A dipolar modulation appears to be present for the higher energies considered as well, and at the highest energies, i.e. above 32 EeV, we find indications of its coexistence with an overdensity of intermediate angular scale, located in the Centaurus region.
authors: J. R. T. de Mello Neto

title: Spectral-Timing Evolution of the Black Hole X-ray Binary LMC X-3: An XPoSat View
summary: LMC X-3 is a persistent black hole high-mass X-ray binary and serves as an important laboratory for studying accretion disk evolution across different spectral states. We present a spectral-timing analysis of XPoSat/XSPECT observations of LMC X--3 obtained during 2024 and 2025. Using broadband X-ray light curves, hardness diagnostics, power spectral analysis, and spectral modeling, we investigate the long-term evolution of the source across multiple epochs. LMC X-3 exhibits significant changes in both its spectral and timing properties between the two observing campaigns. Hardness-intensity and hardness-rms diagrams reveal a clear separation between the 2024 and 2025 observations and even within the 2024 observations. Overall, it indicates a transition from a relatively harder and more variable state to a brighter, softer, and less variable state. Power spectral analysis shows enhanced broadband variability during the 2024 observations, while the 2025 observations are characterized by weaker variability. Spectral modeling of the combined XSPECT observations indicates an increase in the thermal disk temperature from 0.8 to 1.17 keV, accompanied by a ~5 times increase in X-ray flux between the two epochs. The observed reduction in fractional rms variability with increasing source brightness and decreasing spectral hardness is consistent with more contribution from a stable thermal accretion disk. Taken together, the spectral and timing diagnostics provide a self-consistent picture of accretion-state evolution in LMC X-3, demonstrating the capability of XSPECT to probe long-term variability and accretion processes in bright black hole X-ray binaries.

title: A large radiatively loud anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586 with a protracted recovery
summary: Context. Anti-glitches are rare and enigmatic timing anomalies. High-cadence monitoring has revealed radiatively quiet anti-glitches in several pulsar populations, but radiatively loud anti-glitches and their links to magnetospheric activity remain poorly understood. Aims. We characterize a new, large anti-glitch in the magnetar 1E 2259+586 and compare its phenomenology with other magnetars. Methods. We analyze timing, flux, pulse-profile evolution, and spectra using EP, NICER, and IXPE X-ray observations. Results. We report a 2025 anti-glitch in 1E 2259+586, the largest in this source, with $Δν\approx-1.174(7)\times10^{-7}$ Hz and $Δν/ν\approx-8.19(4)\times10^{-7}$. Unlike its 2019 anti-glitch, this event was radiatively loud: the persistent X-ray flux roughly doubled (~106% increase), followed by a recovery exceeding 320 days. The pulse profile changed modestly but significantly: the valley between the main and secondary peaks became shallower and then recovered with the flux. Spectral properties also changed, and Fermi-GBM detected a short soft gamma-ray burst near the event. These features resemble the radiatively loud 2012 anti-glitch. Conclusions. 1E 2259+586 is unique among magnetars: its anti-glitch rate is comparable to normal spin-up glitch rates, and its anti-glitches can be radiatively loud or relatively quiescent. The fractional anti-glitch amplitudes appear to increase monotonically; further verification is needed. Regular monitoring of 1E 2259+586 is essential for understanding anti-glitch mechanisms.

title: Stellar Scalar Monopoles from Gauss--Bonnet Curvature beyond Four Dimensions
summary: Above four dimensions every static, spherically symmetric star, isotropic or anisotropic, carries a scalar monopole at first order in a scalar--Gauss--Bonnet coupling, given by an interior integral weighted by the energy density plus radial pressure. Under the radial null energy condition its sign is that of the coupling for any equation of state, opposite to that of a Schwarzschild--Tangherlini black hole at the same order. The charge is fixed by the lapse-weighted Gauss--Bonnet curvature of space, which vanishes identically when space is three-dimensional.

title: Empirical constraints on cosmic-ray scattering in NGC 1333 from dust polarisation
summary: Cosmic rays (CRs) regulate molecular-cloud ionization and chemistry. Gyro-resonant scattering by magnetic fluctuations sets their mean free path and, on larger scales, their effective diffusion coefficient. However, coefficients inferred from CR distributions averaged over cloud to Galactic scales leave local magnetic structure unresolved. We use the magnetic-field structure of NGC 1333 and its embedded protostellar core IRAS 4A to estimate local CR scattering rates and effective diffusion coefficients, $D(E)$, and examine their variation with environment and scale. We analyse JCMT/POL-2 maps of nine NGC 1333 regions and ALMA Band 7 maps of two IRAS 4A regions. We estimate plane-of-sky field strengths and derive fluctuation spectra from polarisation-angle structure functions. Where these spectra are sufficiently constrained, we apply quasi-linear gyro-resonant theory to calculate CR pitch-angle scattering rates and $D(E)$. The measured fluctuations constrain CR scattering over proton energy intervals of approximately 0.24-5.3 PeV in NGC 1333 and 10-57 TeV in IRAS 4A. Within these intervals, $D(E)$ spans approximately $3\times10^{28}$-$10^{31}\,{\rm cm^2\,s^{-1}}$. Scattering varies substantially between regions and is stronger where the magnetic-field angular dispersion is greater. Extrapolation to common energies suggests scattering in IRAS 4A is one to two orders of magnitude stronger than its surroundings. Within the directly probed intervals, the scattering mean free paths exceed the individual region sizes. The inferred diffusion coefficients therefore characterise local scattering conditions. A cloud-scale diffusive regime requires CRs to sample multiple regions with different scattering rates. Dust polarisation observations therefore provide constraints on CR scattering in clouds, connecting scattering to cloud-scale transport at energies accessible to $γ$-ray observatories.

title: Search Method for Continuous Gravitational Waves from Rotating Neutron Stars in Highly Eccentric Wide Orbits
summary: Recent results from the Gaia third data release have highlighted 21 potential neutron stars candidates in wide, highly-eccentric binary systems and provide estimates of their orbital parameters. We present a feasibility study for a directed search for continuous gravitational waves (CWs) tailored for these and similar systems. To this extent, we have computed a frequency metric to place templates in the parameter space accounting for uncertainties on the orbital parameters. We have built upon the FastTracks infrastructure to efficiently tackle the high-dimensional search space, leveraging a combination of downsampling and interpolation to reduce the computational cost of generating the binary Doppler correction. We performed an injection campaign to demonstrate the performance of this procedure and showed that a search using this approach is viable. Such a search would represent the first combination of Gaia observations and CW analysis.

title: NuSTAR view of the NGC 4151 corona: thermal balance and astroparticle constraints
summary: I present a comprehensive analysis of all publicly available NuSTAR observations of the nearby Seyfert galaxy NGC 4151 (2012--2024). The hard X-ray continuum is well described by thermal Comptonization in a hot corona, with electron temperatures $kT_{\rm e} \approx 40-125$ keV and optical depths $τ\approx 0.4-1.2$ (slab geometry). A clear anti-correlation between $kT_{\rm e}$ and $τ$ is observed, consistent with a thermostat behavior with constant Compton parameter $γ\approx 3.12$ calculated according to Sunyaev and Titarchuk (1980). Variability on timescales of hours constrains the size of the emitting region to $R \approx 250-1200 r_{\rm g}$, corresponding to moderate compactness values $\ell \lesssim 4$. The source occupies the same region of the compactness--temperature plane as other local Seyferts, with no evidence for pair runaway. I then explore two astroparticle implications. The IceCube neutrino excess reported toward NGC 4151 corresponds to $L_ν/L_X \approx 0.3\%$, an energetically negligible contribution that does not alter the observed coronal energy balance. An additional injection of pairs from the hypothetical X17 boson cannot produce significant changes, unless the injection rate exceeds the photoproduction one, but no anomalies were found in the present data set. The NuSTAR data thus provide no evidence for either a significant neutrino cooling channel or an X17-related pair injection in the corona of NGC 4151.

title: Response of Circular Binaries to Monochromatic Gravitational Waves
summary: The exchange in specific orbital energy between a test particle in a Keplerian binary orbit and a continuously incident linearized gravitational wave (GW) is considered. Analytical expressions for the rate of change of energy, semi-major axis and mean motion of the test particle are derived. Numerical solutions illustrate a resonance effect betwen the GWs frequency and the particle's initial orbital frequency. We distinguish between bounded short-period oscillations and resonant libration. The effect of the GWs angle of incidence with the particle's orbital plane is also considered. Using an illustrative high GW strain we show that changes to the eccentricity are bounded while inclination exhibits small linear growth for an initially flat, circular orbit. Long coherence requirements linit the observational significance of GW resonance to astrophysical systems with very short orbital periods.

title: Two-component $γ$-Ray Structure from the CR Sources
summary: With the advent of a new generation of observational experiments and the accumulation of data, an increasing number of cosmic-ray sources have been found to exhibit pronounced two-component structures in their gamma-ray spectra above GeV energies. To investigate whether these structures share a common physical origin, we conduct a statistical study of sources exhibiting such features using a two-component model of cosmic-ray sources and examine their gamma-ray emission mechanisms. We find that the ambient environment significantly affects the spectral morphology. Sources located in low-density environments but surrounded by dense molecular clumps exhibit two clearly separated spectral peaks. In contrast, sources embedded in dense environments with additional dense molecular clumps nearby retain two-component spectral features, but the components overlap more smoothly, with the high-energy component appearing primarily as a relatively broad shoulder rather than a distinct peak. Our results lend further support to a physical picture in which high-energy cosmic rays are predominantly supplied by local sources, whereas low-energy cosmic rays arise mainly from the collective contribution of sources in other regions of the Galaxy. We also calculate the neutrino spectra of these sources, providing theoretical predictions for future tests of the model through observations of point-source and diffuse neutrino emission.

title: Renormalized dynamical tidal response of neutron stars in binary dynamics
summary: We present the relativistic dynamical tidal response of a neutron star computed using stellar perturbation theory and matched to a worldline effective field theory via the tidal scattering phase. This phase is defined as the difference between the Compton/Raman scattering phase of gravitational-waves from a neutron star and the real part of the black hole scattering phase. The gravitational corrections to the response function are obtained using self-energy corrections up to fourth post-Minkowskian order. The response function for neutron stars obeying the BSk22 equation-of-state from Brussels-Skyrme family, is then consistently matched to an effective theory of relativistic quadrupolar harmonic oscillators to model the fundamental-mode ($f$-mode) and low-frequency gravity-modes ($g$-modes). This matching includes the frequency and tidal coupling of each mode and the post-adiabatic dynamical tidal Love number, and once matched this model is in excellent agreement with the full neutron star response. With the external tidal field up to third post-Newtonian order, we also analyse the tidal coupling of the induced quadrupole on the neutron star in a circular binary system, and the adiabatic binding energy.

title: Landau Theory of Black-Brane Phase Transitions from Kasner Singularities
summary: We develop a Landau theory of a continuous black-brane phase transition using the geometry of the black-hole interior. The normal phase has a Reissner--Nordström Cauchy horizon, whereas the scalarized phase ends at a Kasner singularity. A conserved radial charge determines the grand potential from either endpoint and permits a direct phase comparison. At the critical point, we show analytically that the quadratic correction to the conserved radial charge vanishes. Using the inverse Kasner scalar velocity as an interior order parameter, we then construct a Landau potential whose coefficients are determined entirely from the terminal singularity. The Iyer--Wald first law relates this potential to the conventional boundary Landau theory and fixes its quartic coefficient. For two models with different scalar self-interactions, the resulting theory predicts the critical scaling of the Kasner order parameter and the grand-potential difference between the phases, in agreement with fully backreacted numerical solutions.

title: Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays require metal-rich sources
summary: The elemental composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) must be evaluated at a given rigidity rather than energy to compare with candidate elemental abundances, such as those of low-energy cosmic rays seeding the acceleration of UHECRs. We determine the UHECR composition from fits to Pierre Auger Observatory data and evaluate the resulting abundances at fixed rigidity. We identify two classes of solutions consistent with measurements above $10^{17.8}$ eV: one in which the hydrogen flux at Earth is dominated by secondary nucleons produced by photodisintegration of heavier nuclei in extragalactic photon fields, and a second in which this contribution is less pronounced. Only the latter, which yields a mixture of primary and secondary protons at Earth, allows a hydrogen abundance at the source comparable to that of low-energy cosmic rays. However, both classes of solutions require an overabundance of nuclei in the silicon-iron group. Other source models from the literature also fail to reproduce the full elemental composition. The metallicity of UHECRs thus differs markedly from that of all candidate seed populations considered, leaving the origin of the heavy-element excess unresolved.

title: Gravitational Origin of Black Hole Thermodynamic Geometry from Boundary Conditions
summary: In black hole thermodynamics, Hessian metrics change both their signature and their singularities from one statistical ensemble to another. A negative eigenvalue may therefore signal either a physical instability or only a Legendre transformation. We derive this geometry from the bulk action and boundary terms of four-dimensional Euclidean Einstein-Maxwell-anti-de Sitter gravity. In the bulk, the radial symplectic flux pairs the mass and charge with their asymptotic sources, and horizon regularity selects the equilibrium states. At infinity, the boundary terms determine the ensemble polarization by specifying which reservoir parameters are held constant and which conjugate quantities fluctuate. Fixing the temperature and electric potential gives the Ruppeiner metric, whereas adding the Maxwell boundary term fixes the charge and reverses the corresponding metric sign. Tracking the boundary conditions thus separates true stability boundaries from singularities of the Legendre transform. Local holographic counterterms leave the metric unchanged, while mixed electric boundary conditions interpolate between the two ensembles and shift their stability limits.

title: Constraints on Lorentz Invariance Violation from PeV Gamma Rays of Cygnus X-3 Observed by LHAASO
summary: The Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO) has detected photons with energies up to 3.7 PeV from the binary system Cygnus X-3 during a flaring episode. The combination of such extreme photon energies and the large source distance provides a sensitive probe of Lorentz invariance violation (LIV). In superluminal LIV scenarios, high-energy photons can become unstable and rapidly decay, resulting in a sharp spectral cutoff. However, the observed hard intrinsic spectrum of Cygnus X-3 exhibits no evidence for such a feature. This absence enables us to place stringent constraints on LIV, with the second-order LIV energy scale constrained to be above 10^{-2}M_{pl}, improving previous limits by nearly an order of magnitude.

title: Non-singular cosmology from effective LQG-inspired black holes
summary: We propose a non-singular primordial cosmology derived from matching an effective Loop Quantum Gravity-inspired black hole geometry to an expanding Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker universe via Darmois-Israel junction conditions. The resulting modified Friedmann equation replaces the singularity with a quantum bounce in the Planckian regime. Mapping the surface energy-momentum tensor of the dynamic thin shell onto a homogeneous scalar field reveals a transient phantom-like behavior. For any equation of state of the shell satisfying $ω> -1$, its effective energy density is diluted with cosmic expansion. Extending the framework to a two-scalar-field system provides a mechanism to bridge the energy gap between the Planckian bounce and the sub-Planckian scale. The pre-inflationary phase is brief, enabling the second scalar field to take over to drive the standard slow-roll inflation.

title: Inverse Scattering & Isospectrality in (Analog) Cosmology
summary: Cosmological particle production, the excitation of field quanta by a dynamical spacetime, underlies the primordial perturbations observed in the cosmic microwave background and has been realized in analog quantum simulators with ultra-cold atoms. We ask the inverse question: given the excitation spectrum, can the cosmological history that produced it be reconstructed, and is that reconstruction unique? We approach this problem through a mapping of particle production to one-dimensional quantum scattering, in which the expansion history plays the role of a scattering landscape and the produced spectrum the role of reflected and transmitted waves. This mapping reveals a rich interplay between scattering theory and cosmology. The scale factor enters as a zero-energy resonance, an exceptional case of scattering theory, while cosmic singularities correspond to bound states, so that regular cosmologies are governed entirely by the scattering continuum. We find an interesting isospectrality: histories related by an inversion of the scale factor (expansion <-> contraction) yield identical particle numbers, differing only by a pi-shift in phase. Given both the particle number (or alternatively the amplitude) and phase of the cosmological power spectrum, the reconstruction is unique for regular, asymptotically static cosmologies. We demonstrate the reconstruction both analytically, for exactly solvable scattering landscapes, and numerically, recovering common logistic expansion histories to better than 0.02%. We further quantify its robustness to the momentum-space resolution and measurement uncertainties characteristic of analog quantum simulation. This work establishes a direct link between the observable power spectrum and the cosmological history that produced it, offering a new perspective on the classification of early-universe scenarios and the construction of alternatives to inflation.

title: Gravitational Particle Production and Locality of the Wavefunction-Squared
summary: We show that no particle production due to the background geometry implies the locality of the wavefunction-squared for free heavy masses on expanding cosmologies. On global de Sitter of odd dimensions these two stem from the same identity, whereas in the Poincare patch neither occur under any condition. These two phenomena both depend on the behaviour of the out modes at far future and we show that they almost always come together for systems with an out mode that has a phase with separated time and momentum dependency at far future. This will be true for most expanding cosmologies. We comment on how the discussion can be connected to Green's functions and on some previous results in the literature that are seemingly contrary to our conclusions.

title: Log-normal behavior of Optical Polarization in a sample of Blazars: Evidence for Multiplicative Magneto-hydrodynamic Processes in Relativistic Jets
summary: Optical synchrotron polarization is one of the most direct probes of the magnetic-field structure and particle-acceleration processes in the relativistic jets of blazars. Although long-term optical flux variability is often attributed to multiplicative stochastic processes because of its log-normal behavior, but the physical origin of optical polarization variability remains less understood. In this study, we investigate the long-term optical flux and polarization variability of a sample of blazars using nearly a decade of photo-polarimetric observations from the Steward Observatory. We find that, like the optical flux, the optical degree of polarization is generally well described by a log-normal distribution and shows an approximately linear relationship between its variability amplitude and mean value. We interpret this behavior within a magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) framework in which the magnetic-field undergoes repeated stochastic changes driven by shocks, turbulence, velocity shear, and large-scale jet dynamics. The cumulative effect of these processes can naturally generate multiplicative variability, leaving similar statistical signatures in both the synchrotron flux and the degree of polarization. Our results provide new observational evidence that the long-term statistical behavior of optical flux and polarization may arise from a common set of MHD processes associated with magnetic-field evolution.

title: Cross-experiment tests of the atmospheric-muon excess
summary: High-energy cosmic rays produce atmospheric muons through cascades of hadronic interactions, yet simulations often underestimate the muon content of extensive air showers. Whether the same problem affects energetic atmospheric muons, which probe a different part of the cascade, is less clear. Here we compare published atmospheric-muon measurements from four experiments with reference predictions based on a shared choice of hadronic interaction model and primary cosmic-ray flux. We find that the measurements predominantly exceed the central predictions across different experimental techniques, from surface measurements to deep detectors. This recurring excess is more consistent across the measurements than any inferred dependence on energy or zenith angle. These atmospheric muons preferentially originate from energetic mesons produced early in the cascade, whereas the total muon content of extensive air showers also reflects interactions at later stages. A common explanation of both excesses must therefore increase the effective supply of energetic muon parents, rather than merely increasing the multiplicity of soft particles. This provides a way to distinguish between competing explanations of the cosmic-ray muon puzzle.

title: Active learning at a graduate summer school: feasibility, student response, and the role of instructor training
summary: Active learning is becoming standard practice in undergraduate STEM instruction in North America and is slowly being adopted in graduate courses. Graduate summer schools, one- to two-week programs in which students from many institutions gather for intensive, specialized instruction in their field, are common in physics; they are taught by researchers chosen for their expertise, and their pedagogy remains almost entirely traditional lecturing. We report a study at a one-week graduate school in neutrino and astroparticle physics attended by 38 students from 8 countries. Six lecturers with limited or no prior experience of teaching with active learning introduced Peer Instruction-style active learning into their lectures after approximately four hours of preparation led by a physics-education specialist. Each of the three main lecture streams was taught traditionally on one day and in the active format on the other. Students were surveyed after each of the first two days and at the end of the week; all six instructors were surveyed as well. In every active lecture, spanning three instructors and three topics, 82-100% of respondents reported that the interactive segments helped them stay engaged and check their understanding, and in every stream the difficulty was rated as better matched on the active day. At the end of the week, 33 of 36 wanted such teaching in future graduate courses, and not one respondent disagreed. All six instructors judged the approach productive and intend to use it again; only two found implementation straightforward. With brief expert-led preparation, lecturers new to active learning implemented it successfully for a heterogeneous audience, and both students and instructors want more. The school was also the first time any of the six instructors implemented structured active learning: a summer school can develop its lecturers as well as its students.

title: Quasinormal overtones and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes
summary: We investigate scalar quasinormal modes (QNMs), with particular attention to overtones, and grey-body factors of Frolov black holes, which interpolate between the Reissner--Nordström (RN) and Hayward limits. Over the allowed ranges of charge $q$ and regularization parameter $α_0$, all QNM frequencies have negative imaginary parts, confirming stability against scalar perturbations. Increasing either $q$ or $α_0$ can trigger overtone outbursts, with the Frolov threshold shifted to smaller parameter values than in the RN or Hayward cases. Angular momentum does not eliminate the outburst but postpones its onset from $n=1$ at $l=0$ to $n\geq 2$ at $l=1$. Comparisons of the effective potential show that, for $l=1$, charge raises the barrier peak much more strongly than $α_0$, while the clearest deviations from the Hayward and RN references are localized near the horizon. Using the QNM--grey-body correspondence at $l=1$, we find that overtone corrections are essential, and the amended formula substantially outperforms the eikonal truncation. At fixed frequency, both $q$ and $α_0$ suppress transmission, with charge being the dominant factor, consistent with the stronger barrier enhancement under the charge scan.

title: AGN feedback destroying group cool cores --- a case study on IC 2476 with a remnant radio AGN and an exceptionally low abundance
summary: We present results from deep XMM-Newton observations ($\sim$180 ksec) of the galaxy group IC 2476 in the X-GAP sample, capturing a rare AGN feedback regime, where the central radio AGN has ceased activity but the radio lobes are still detectable. The hot intragroup medium of IC 2476 features a compact cool core, with a size of ~10 kpc, and a moderate X-ray luminosity of $\sim3.4\times10^{40}$ erg/s. We measured an unusually low temperature of $\sim$0.45 keV within the cool core. We measured an exceptionally low abundance of below ~0.2 solar, even in the central region. The X-ray surface brightness of the group is not symmetric and shows a clear depression in the region overlaid with the eastern radio lobe, suggesting the presence of an X-ray cavity. The scaled entropy of the hot gas within 0.1 r500 of IC 2476 is among the highest in X-ray galaxy groups with a similar system temperature. Our study suggests that the past powerful radio AGN outburst in IC 2476 has disrupted the cool core and the X-ray cavity has dissipated or mixed with the surrounding hot gas since the shutdown of the central AGN. A large cool core may be gradually re-established in the absence of AGN activity. This system therefore provides a great example of AGN feedback destroying the group cool core, even with a moderate radio luminosity at present.

title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) are described by second-order tensor perturbations that contain free radiation together with a gauge-dependent response maintained by the scalar source. For a perfect fluid with constant equation of state $0<w<1$, we identify the free radiation with the out-state of the tensor perturbation, assembled from the light-cone residue of kernel functions for each pair of scalar modes. Its amplitudes follow from a classical LSZ-type reduction formula, in terms of the initial data and the light-cone-projected source. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: a redefinition of the tensor perturbation whose late-time shift has power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leaves these amplitudes unchanged. Transformations between intrinsic gauges, whose slice-normal observers and spatial coordinates are fixed by the matter and geometry without an external clock or independent oscillatory dynamics, are redefinitions of this kind, except on resonance surfaces of zero measure. The out-state is therefore the same in all intrinsic gauges, including the standard gauges of cosmological perturbation theory. The late-time Newtonian kernel is then the out-state kernel, which justifies its use for the energy spectrum of the free radiation. In matter domination, the out-state instead separates the free radiation from the static tidal response.

title: A dual-moment framework toward unification of the four fundamental interactions
summary: The unification of the four fundamental interactions remains one of the central open challenges in fundamental physics. Most existing unification scenarios rely on extra spatial dimensions, novel symmetry structures, or unobserved dynamical degrees of freedom. In this work, we construct a minimal phenomenological dual-moment framework rooted in primitive charges and motion-induced kinetic moments. Gravitational, electromagnetic, and strong interactions are coherently described within a unified inverse-square-law formalism. We postulate a universal coupling relation $T = Z/c^2$ that connects source-charge coupling coefficients and moment-mediated coupling coefficients across different interaction sectors. While the framework can formally accommodate weak-charge degrees of freedom, full quantitative computations for weak-interaction dynamics are deferred to future follow-up studies. The model reproduces established low-energy dynamical limits for planetary orbits, atomic systems, and heavy-quark hadrons, and predicts distinguishable corrections to light deflection by rapidly spinning compact objects. We further design three independent test schemes: improved torsion-balance measurements, a mass-current laboratory deflection experiment, and astronomical light-bending observations. Although laboratory measurements impose formidable technical challenges, astronomical observations of compact spinning objects offer promising avenues to constrain or falsify the proposed framework.

title: Flux Variation of the Crab Pulsar Observed Using Fermi LAT and NuSTAR
summary: The flux of pulsed emission from the Crab pulsar, just like most of other pulsars, is considered to be steady over time scales much larger than the pulsation period, except for a smooth, secular decrease related to the aging of pulsars. Such a steady assumption prevails in all theoretical investigations of pulsar emission models. However, here we report the discovery of stochastic fluctuation in the flux and photon index of the Crab pulsar gamma-ray and X-ray emissions utilizing archival data of Fermi LAT (0.1 -- 100 GeV, spanning 17 years) and of NuSTAR (3.0 -- 79.0 keV, spanning 13 years) observations. The origin of such fluctuation is intriguing. It might be related to possible configuration adjustment of magnetic fields in neutron stars' superconducting and superfluid interiors.
